blogs.title: When the Pancreas Invades the Pleura: Recognizing Pancreatopleural Fistula in Kids
blogs.description: A deep dive into the clinical clues that should raise suspicion for a pancreatopleural fistula in children—recurrent hemorrhagic pleural effusions, high pleural amylase, and a hidden history of abdominal trauma. We’ll outline a step‑by‑step diagnostic algorithm that integrates bedside thoracentesis, fluid analysis, and targeted imaging (CT, MRCP) to avoid costly missteps such as empiric TB therapy.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase: A ‘Water‑Test’ for Hidden Pancreatic Leaks
blogs.description: Explores the utility of pleural fluid amylase (and lipase) measurement in differentiating pancreatopleural fistula from common pediatric pleural effusion etiologies (TB, empyema, malignancy, Boerhaave). The post will discuss amylase iso‑typing, threshold values, and how a single lab result can steer clinicians toward abdominal imaging rather than endless pulmonary work‑ups.

blogs.title: Conservative Management of Pediatric Pancreatopleural Fistula: Octreotide, NPO, and TPN
blogs.description: Reviews the medical management armamentarium for PPF—bowel rest, total parenteral nutrition, somatostatin analogues, and pancreatic enzyme replacement. We’ll examine dosing strategies, duration of therapy, success rates in children (≈12%), and practical tips for monitoring drainage, nutrition, and potential complications.

blogs.title: When to Move Beyond Medicine: Endoscopic and Surgical Options for Refractory PPF
blogs.description: Analyzes the decision‑making pathway from failed conservative therapy to ERCP‑guided stenting and, if needed, definitive surgery (distal pancreatectomy, Puestow, cystojejunostomy). The article will compare outcomes, success rates, and procedural risks in the pediatric population, offering a flowchart for clinicians faced with persistent fistula drainage.

blogs.title: The ‘Pulmonary Mask’ of Abdominal Trauma: Lessons from a Hidden Pancreatic Leak
blogs.description: Uses this case to highlight how blunt abdominal injury can masquerade as a primary respiratory problem. It will discuss epidemiology of trauma‑induced pancreatitis in children, the anatomical routes (aortic vs. esophageal hiatus) by which pancreatic fluid reaches the pleural space, and strategies for obtaining a comprehensive history even when patients conceal trauma.

blogs.title: Genetics vs. Trauma: Etiological Spectrum of Pediatric Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: Contrasts the predominant causes of PPF in adults (alcoholic chronic pancreatitis) with those in children (hereditary mutations, blunt trauma). The post will overview key genetic mutations (PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR), when to pursue genetic testing, and how etiologic insight influences long‑term management and counseling.
